_meta.indication: EMFLAZA is indicated for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in patients 5 years of age and older.

pivotal_trials.phase: Not stated (a specific clinical trial phase is not designated in the review; the study is described as a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled study)
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 52-week study evaluating two deflazacort dosing levels (0.9 or 1.2 mg/kg/day) and one prednisone level, conducted in the US and Canada.
pivotal_trials.population: 196 male pediatric patients 5 to 15 years of age with onset of weakness before 5 years of age (DMD)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from Baseline to Week 12 in muscle strength of 18 muscle groups, assessed by the 11-point modified Medical Research Council (MRC) muscle strength assessment
pivotal_trials.n: 196 patients (deflazacort 0.9 mg/kg/day N=49, deflazacort 1.2 mg/kg/day N=48, prednisone N=46, placebo N=50 in the reviewer's primary-endpoint analysis)
pivotal_trials.result: Change in average muscle strength from Baseline to Week 12 was significantly greater than placebo: deflazacort 0.9 mg/kg/day between-treatment difference 0.25 (95% CI 0.06, 0.44), p=0.0047; deflazacort 1.2 mg/kg/day difference 0.36 (95% CI 0.17, 0.55), p<0.0001.

pivotal_trials.phase: Not stated (a specific clinical trial phase is not designated in the review; described as a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled supportive trial)
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, 104-week trial conducted in Italy
pivotal_trials.population: 29 male children 6 to 12 years of age with DMD confirmed by abnormal dystrophin or a confirmed dystrophin gene mutation
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change in muscle strength from baseline to Year 2 or loss of ambulation, whichever occurred first (MRC index score)
pivotal_trials.result: Primary endpoint (change at Year 2) was not statistically significant, likely due to few remaining placebo patients; muscle strength numerically favored deflazacort earlier (Month 6 difference 6.97, p=0.0192; Year 1 difference 8.53, p=0.0056). Median time to loss of ambulation 63 months for deflazacort vs 32 months for placebo (p=0.0052).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10% and greater than placebo) are Cushingoid appearance, weight increased, increased appetite, upper respiratory tract infection, cough, pollakiuria, hirsutism, central obesity, and nasopharyngitis. At 12 weeks: Cushingoid appearance 33% vs 12% placebo, weight increased 20% vs 6%, increased appetite 14% vs 2%. A range of psychiatric adverse events (abnormal behavior 6.8%, irritability 5.1%, aggression 4%) and cases consistent with toxic epidermal necrolysis were reported.
target_moa: Deflazacort is a corticosteroid prodrug whose active metabolite, 21-desDFZ, acts through the glucocorticoid receptor to exert anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects; the precise mechanism of benefit in DMD is unknown.

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary and there were no issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion.

summary.text: Deflazacort (Emflaza) was submitted as 505(b)(2) NDAs, received June 9, 2016, and received a full approval on the first cycle for DMD in patients 5 years and older. It held Orphan Drug designation (2013), Fast Track designation (2014), Rare Pediatric Disease designation (2015), and priority review, and the sponsor was granted a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher.

citations.quote: Although originally submitted as 505(b)(1) applications, both NDAs were changed to 505(b)(2) applications, based on use by the applicant of published literature.

The Agency granted Orphan Drug designation to deflazacort for the treatment of DMD on August 16, 2013, and Fast Track designation on November 21, 2014. Marathon requested Rare Pediatric Disease designation on March 20, 2015, which was granted on August 10, 2015.
Deflazacort was granted a priority review designation for this application.
We also inform you that you have been granted a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher, as provided under section 529 of the FDCA.
